title: Who's Who: Sofia Renard
summary: Field physician whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Sofia Renard (1824–1881) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a field physician whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Renard first described referential fatigue as a measurable alteration in objects exposed to sustained sonance. Her 1863 case records include garments that no longer fit their owners and tools that would not perform familiar tasks.
She argued for controlled storage of retrievals while resisting sensational claims about transformed people.

For Alderwick readers, Sofia Renard is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
